name: WP2 — Runner tick and background worker (resumable, single worker, budget hard stop)
description:
Third work package of LRT-1. Design contract: docs/long-running-tasks.md · Plan: docs/long-running-tasks-plan.md §2 WP2. Depends on WP1.

OBJECTIVE
Advance a run by exactly one durable step at a time, from the BACKGROUND process, and survive a restart without a manual resume.

SCOPE
1. codx/junior/long_running/runner.py — LongRunningRunner.tick(project, main_task_id):
   - acquire the WP1 RunLock; refresh the heartbeat; do nothing if the lock is not ours;
   - reload the main task from disk every tick (nothing kept in memory);
   - stop conditions checked in this order: run_status != running -> exit; spent >= budget -> run_status="budget_exhausted" + write the delivery report; remaining <= supervisor_reserve -> same;
   - pick ONE actionable task: board == run board, root_id == main task id, status in (todo, doing), attempts < 3, order by priority, due_date, sort_index;
   - before the turn set the task estimation_cost = min(per_task_budget, remaining - supervisor_reserve); run session.chat_with_project(chat=task);
   - persist attempts/current_task_id/step_started_at/last_tick_at/ticks after every unit;
   - recovery: current_task_id set + no CANCELLATION_REGISTRY token -> attempts += 1 and re-run; after 3 attempts set status="onhold" and leave a request_help comment;
   - nothing actionable -> one supervisor turn on the MAIN TASK using the run profile to create/move/verify tasks, or to call finish; a turn that neither creates nor moves a task increments stagnation; stagnation >= 3 -> run_status="stalled".
2. codx/junior/background.py — check_long_running_runs() + run_long_running_tick(), own daemon thread started in start_background_services() next to check_projects(), guarded by the same stop event, ~5s interval, one thread per run with asyncio.run(). This must only run in the process started with CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND.
3. Honoured cancellation: pause/stop read from disk before the turn AND CANCELLATION_REGISTRY.cancel(current_task_id) visible mid-turn.

ACCEPTANCE (evidence required in the task report)
- Two simulated workers never process the same run twice (lock evidence).
- Kill the worker mid-run and restart: the same tick resumes with no manual action and attempts is incremented by exactly 1.
- pause before the turn -> nothing runs; stop during a turn -> the in-flight token is cancelled and run_status == "stopped".
- A run can never exceed budget in the arithmetic of tick admission (show the numbers).
- The API process (without CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND) starts no long-running thread.

RULES
- One task turn at a time per run (no max_parallel yet).
- Never block the request path; tick() is called only from the background loop (or the manual /tick endpoint added in WP3).
- Use planning_manager constants for status vocabulary.

Two findings that change what I can hand over — both documented at the end. """ Long-running runner — advances a run by **exactly one durable step per tick**. LRT-1 / work package 2. Design contract: ``docs/long-running-tasks.md`` §5, plan: ``docs/long-running-tasks-plan.md`` §2 (WP2). The runner is the only place that *advances* a run. It is never called from a request path (the API has a 30s middleware timeout): the background loop in :mod:`codx.junior.background` calls :meth:`LongRunningRunner.tick`, or the manual ``POST /api/long-running/{main_task_id}/tick`` endpoint added in WP3. Shape of a tick --------------- ```mermaid flowchart TD T[tick] --> L{RunLock acquired?} L -->|no| X[skip: locked] L -->|yes| S{run_status == running?} S -->|no| X2[skip] S -->|yes| B{budget configured?} B -->|no| F[failed: budget_not_configured] B -->|yes| D{remaining > reserve?} D -->|no| BE[budget_exhausted + report] D -->|yes| R[recover interrupted unit] R --> E[reap exhausted tasks] E --> A{actionable task?} A -->|yes| C[claim task · estimation_cost = min per_task, remaining-reserve
chat_with_project · attempts += 1] C --> T2[next tick] A -->|no| SUP[supervisor turn on the MAIN task] SUP --> G{moved / created / finished?} G -->|finished| CP[completed] G -->|no| ST[stagnation += 1 · stalled at 3] G -->|yes| T2 ST --> T2 ``` Durability rules (this is what makes a restart transparent) ---------------------------------------------------------- 1. **Nothing is kept in memory between ticks.** The main task is reloaded from disk at the start of every tick and before every unit. 2. **The run state lives on the main task** (``Chat.run`` / ``Chat.run_status`` / ``Chat.run_state``), which is persisted after *every* unit. 3. **Only one worker advances a run at a time**: the WP1 ``RunLock`` (own file, ``O_CREAT|O_EXCL`` + heartbeat + stale takeover) is acquired before anything else. A second worker (another thread, another process) sees it and skips. 4. **The in-flight unit is a single ``chat_with_project`` turn**, which is itself persisted incrementally by ``ChatEventBridge``. If the process dies mid-turn, ``run_state["current_task_id"]`` survives and the next tick re-runs the same task — no manual "resume" click. Budget arithmetic (hard stop, never exceeded) --------------------------------------------- Admission happens *before* a turn, using the values on disk:: budget = main.estimation_cost # declared on the MAIN task spent = max(main.cost, Σ descendants) # cost rolls up into the root remaining = budget - spent supervisor_reserve = run["supervisor_reserve"] turn_cap = min(run["per_task_budget"], remaining - supervisor_reserve) # numbers: budget 10.0, spent 6.5, reserve 1.5, per_task 2.0 remaining = 3.5 -> remaining > reserve (1.5) -> run a turn turn_cap = min(2.0, 2.0) = 2.0 -> task capped at 2.0 # worst case after the turn: spent = 8.5, remaining = 1.5 == reserve # -> next tick stops as budget_exhausted and writes the report # WITHOUT paying for another LLM turn (template, no AI call) ``spent`` is recomputed from the chats on every tick; the persisted counter is never trusted (drift protection). The roll-up (WP1 / LRT-0.4) makes ``main.cost`` the run total, and ``max()`` keeps the arithmetic conservative if the roll-up ever fails for a child. Contract consumed from WP1 (``codx/junior/long_running``) -------------------------------------------------------- * ``models.LongRunStatus`` — ``running``/``paused``/``stopped``/``completed``/ ``budget_exhausted``/``failed``/``stalled``. * ``store.LongRunStore(settings)`` with ``lock(main_task_id)`` returning a ``RunLock`` exposing ``acquire() -> bool``, ``heartbeat() -> None`` and ``release() -> None`` (stale takeover handled inside the lock). * ``db.Chat`` fields ``run`` (config dict), ``run_status`` (str) and ``run_state`` (dict: ``attempts``, ``current_task_id``, ``step_started_at``, ``last_tick_at``, ``ticks``, ``stagnation``, ``stop_reason``, ``finished``). MAX_ATTEMPTS: int = 3 # Consecutive supervisor turns that neither create nor move a task. STAGNATION_TICKS: int = 3 # Defaults, overridable through Chat.run (WP1 fills them when the run starts). DEFAULT_PER_TASK_BUDGET: float = 1.0 DEFAULT_SUPERVISOR_RESERVE: float = 0.5 DEFAULT_MAX_TASKS: int = 50 DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS: int = 300 # Lock heartbeat before each long operation (the lock itself decides staleness). LOCK_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS: float = 30.0 # How often a running turn re-reads the main task to honour pause/stop. STATUS_POLL_SECONDS: float = 2.0 # Suffix marker stored in meta_data of the messages this runner writes. """ SUPERVISOR_PROMPT = """ {objective} budget={budget:.4f} spent={spent:.4f} remaining={remaining:.4f} reserve={reserve:.4f} {tasks} * You are the manager of this run. Decide the next single step and make it happen. * Split the objective into tasks ONLY as deep as needed now. A main task is the **root** of its tree (``root_id`` is itself) and it is the only chat that carries a ``run`` configuration, so descendants are never mistaken for runs. Args: project: Project settings (``CODXJuniorSettings``). Returns: List of main task ids, newest first. Attributes: project: Project settings of the run. _session: Lazily built ``CODXJuniorSession`` (created on first use so a pure discovery pass costs nothing). """ def __init__(self, project=None, session=None): """ Args: project: Project settings; falls back to ``session.settings``. session: Optional pre-built session (reused by the manual tick endpoint in WP3). Raises: ValueError: When neither a project nor a session is given. """ self.project = project or getattr(session, "settings", None) if self.project is None: raise ValueError( "LongRunningRunner requires project settings or a session" ) self._session = session # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Lazy collaborators # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- @property def session(self): """Return (and build on first use) the session used to run turns.""" if self._session is None: from codx.junior.engine import CODXJuniorSession self._session = CODXJuniorSession( settings=self.project, codx_path=self.project.codx_path, ) return self._session @property def chat_manager(self) -> ChatManager: """Return the chat manager of the run's project.""" return self.session.get_chat_manager() @property def store(self) -> LongRunStore: """Return the WP1 run store (state files + cross-process lock).""" return LongRunStore(settings=self.project) @property def events(self): """Return the event manager, when the session exposes one.""" return getattr(self.session, "event_manager", None) # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Public entry point # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- async def tick(self, project=None, main_task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]: """ Advance *main_task_id* by one step. The tick is idempotent and crash-safe: it re-reads the main task from disk, takes the run lock (skipping when another worker holds it) and performs at most **one** unit of work — either one task turn or one supervisor turn. Args: project: Project settings (overrides the instance project, so the background loop can reuse a single runner). main_task_id: Id of the main task (= the run). Returns: A small report of what happened (used by the manual endpoint and by the demo/tests), e.g.:: {"main_task_id": "...", "action": "task", "task_id": "...", "attempt": 1, "spent": 6.5, "remaining": 3.5, "ticks": 12} Raises: ValueError: When *main_task_id* is missing. """ if project is not None and project is not self.project: self.project = project self._session = None main_task_id = (main_task_id or "").strip() if not main_task_id: raise ValueError("tick() requires the main task id") result: Dict[str, Any] = { "main_task_id": main_task_id, "action": "skipped", "reason": None, } lock = self.store.lock(main_task_id) if not lock.acquire(): # Another worker owns this run: exactly what makes the two-worker # case safe (see the acceptance evidence in the task report). result["reason"] = "locked" logger.debug( "long running: run '%s' is locked by another worker, skipping", main_task_id, ) return result try: lock.heartbeat() return await self._tick_locked( main_task_id=main_task_id, lock=lock, result=result ) finally: with contextlib.suppress(Exception): lock.release() # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Tick body # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- async def _tick_locked( self, main_task_id: str, lock, result: Dict[str, Any], ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Run the body of a tick while holding the run lock.""" # 1. Reload from disk: nothing survives between ticks in memory. main = self._load_chat(main_task_id) if main is None: result.update(action="skipped", reason="main_task_not_found") logger.warning("long running: main task '%s' not found", main_task_id) return result run_status = self._run_status(main) if run_status != LongRunStatus.RUNNING.value: result.update(action="skipped", reason=f"run_status={run_status or 'none'}") return result state = self._state(main) state["ticks"] = int(state.get("ticks") or 0) + 1 state["last_tick_at"] = self._now() result["ticks"] = state["ticks"] # 2. Budget admission (before anything is spent). budget = self._budget(main) if budget <= 0: return self._stop( main=main, state=state, status=LongRunStatus.FAILED, reason="budget_not_configured", result=result, ) chats = self._run_chats(main) spent = self._spent(main, chats) remaining = budget - spent reserve = self._reserve(main) result.update(spent=round(spent, 6), remaining=round(remaining, 6)) if remaining <= reserve: return self._stop( main=main, state=state, status=LongRunStatus.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, reason=( f"budget spent ({spent:.4f}/{budget:.4f}); " f"remaining {remaining:.4f} <= reserve {reserve:.4f}" ), result=result, ) # 3. Recover an interrupted unit (crash / power-off mid-turn). self._recover(main=main, state=state) # 4. Park the tasks that exhausted their attempts. self._reap_exhausted(main=main, chats=chats, state=state) # 5. One unit of work: a task turn, or a supervisor turn. task = self._next_task(main=main, chats=chats, state=state) if task is not None: return await self._advance_task( main=main, state=state, task=task, available=remaining - reserve, lock=lock, result=result, ) return await self._supervisor_turn( main=main, state=state, budget=budget, spent=spent, remaining=remaining, reserve=reserve, lock=lock, result=result, ) # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Unit 1 — a task turn # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- async def _advance_task( self, main: Chat, state: Dict[str, Any], task: Chat, available: float, lock, result: Dict[str, Any], ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Run one turn on *task*, bounded by the remaining budget.""" turn_cap = min(self._per_task_budget(main), max(0.0, available)) if turn_cap <= 0: return self._stop( main=main, state=state, status=LongRunStatus.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, reason="no budget left for another task turn", result=result, ) # Claim the unit BEFORE spending: a crash leaves a recoverable trace. state["current_task_id"] = task.id state["step_started_at"] = self._now() state["stagnation"] = 0 self._save_state(main, state) task =

"""
Identity primitives shared by the task / kanban / long-running machinery.

The project rule is: **ids are canonical, names and titles are only labels**.

* every persisted element has an immutable ``id`` (uuid),
* references between elements use ids (``Chat.parent_id``, ``Chat.root_id``,
  ``Chat.kanban_id``, ``Chat.column_id``),
* ``Chat.board`` / ``Chat.column`` / ``Chat.name`` are display labels.

This module owns the primitives the rest of the code must use to reason about
the ancestor chain of a task, so the invariant *"every task of a run shares the
same ancestor (the main task)"* is enforced in one place instead of being
re-implemented (and diverging) by every caller:

* :func:`resolve_root_id` - canonical root (main task) of a chat.
* :func:`is_descendant_of` - guard used by the long-running runner.
* :func:`link_parent` - creation helper used by ``TaskManager``.
* :func:`attach_root_id` - backfill helper.

``Chat.root_id`` is a CACHE of the walk: legacy chats have no value, so the walk
happens once and the result is backfilled on the in-memory chat; the caller
persists it the next time the chat is saved. A cache that is not the chat's own
id is returned without walking (cheap path for every tick of a run).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[chat] --> B{parent_id?}
    B -->|no| C[root_id = chat.id]
    B -->|yes| D{root_id cached?}
    D -->|yes| E[return cache]
    D -->|no| F[walk parent_id up]
    F --> G{cycle or depth limit?}
    G -->|yes| H[stop: log warning, use last chat]
    G -->|no| I[topmost chat reached]
    I --> J[root_id = topmost.id, backfill chat.root_id]
    H --> J
```

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import logging
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Optional

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
    from codx.junior.chat_manager import ChatManager
    from codx.junior.db import Chat

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# A corrupted parent chain must never make the process hang: the walk gives up
# after this many levels (deeper hierarchies are not a realistic task tree).
MAX_PARENT_DEPTH = 64


def attach_root_id(chat: Optional["Chat"], parent_chat: Optional["Chat"] = None) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Compute (and stamp) the ``root_id`` of *chat* from its parent.

    Creation rules:

    * a chat without a parent is its own root (``root_id = chat.id``),
    * a child inherits ``parent.root_id`` when the parent already knows its
      root, and falls back to the parent id otherwise,
    * nothing is inherited from a parent that is not there.

    The value is stamped on the chat itself, so a caller that persists the chat

"""
Shared constants and helpers of the kanban storage.

The kanban catalogue lives in ``<codx_path>/tasks`` and is stored in **v2
format** (see :mod:`codx.junior.kanban.store`):

```
.codx/tasks/
  index.json                       { version: 2, boards: [ {id,title,type,parent_id,folder,order} ], tags }
  boards/<board_id>/board.json     { id,title,description,type,parent_id,folder,columns:[{id,title,color,folder,order}] }
  <folder>/<column_folder>/<slug>.<chat_id>.json
```

``folder`` is **immutable**: it is the name of the directory that holds the
board/column chats. ``title`` is only a label, so renaming a board or a column
changes nothing on disk and no task has to be rewritten.

This module must stay dependency free (no imports from the rest of codx-junior)
because both the store and the migration import it.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import os
import re

# Bumped whenever the on-disk layout changes in a breaking way.
STORE_VERSION = 2

# Version reported by the legacy (v1) single-file layout.
LEGACY_VERSION = 0.1

INDEX_FILE = "index.json"
BOARDS_DIR = "boards"
BOARD_FILE = "board.json"
LEGACY_FILE = "kanban.json"
BACKUP_FILE = "kanban.v1.backup.json"
LOCK_FILE = ".kanban.lock"

DEFAULT_BOARD = "kanban"
DEFAULT_COLUMN = "tasks"
BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN = "kanban"
BOARD_TYPE_SPRINT = "sprint"

# Characters that can never appear in a directory name used as a folder.
_INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS = re.compile(r'[/\\\x00-\x1f]')


def safe_folder(name: str, default: str = "board") -> str:
    """
    Convert a board/column *title* into a directory name.

    The original case and spaces are preserved on purpose: existing projects
    already have folders such as ``To do`` or ``tasks``, and changing them would
    orphan every stored chat.

    Args:
        name: Board or column title.
        default: Value used when the title has no usable characters.

    Returns:
        A path separator free folder name.

    Example:
        >>> safe_folder("To do")
        'To do'
        >>> safe_folder("api/ui")
        'api-ui'
    """
    folder = _INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS.sub("-", str(name or "")).strip()
    folder = folder.strip(".").strip()
    return folder or default


def is_store_file(file_path: str) -> bool:
    """
    Tell whether *file_path* is part of the storage itself (not a chat).

    ``.codx/tasks`` holds both the chats and the catalogue, so any code that
    walks the tree for chats must skip ``index.json``, the legacy
    ``kanban.json`` and everything under ``boards/``.

    Args:
        file_path: Absolute or relative file path.

    Returns:
        True when the path belongs to the kanban storage.
    """
    base = os.path.basename(file_path)
    if base in (INDEX_FILE, LEGACY_FILE, BACKUP_FILE, LOCK_FILE):
        return True
    parts = os.path.normpath(file_path).split(os.sep)
    return BOARDS_DIR in parts

Problem solved
--------------
v1 kept every board of a project in a single ``tasks/kanban.json`` written with
read‑modify‑write and no lock, by the UI *and* by the tools. A concurrent write
dropped boards. v2 keeps:
